gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-biz-udmincho: BIZ UDMincho reads bookish and traditional, a classic serif with a shallow curl at its terminals and plenty of gap between letters. And Arkhip lets its tube-like, neon-glass strokes float above it, so the modern heading and the old-fashioned text feel like two eras sharing a page.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-copse: Arkhip's strokes are as thick as neon tubing and hold that thickness through every bend, with no swelling or thinning. Copse takes the quieter job, a literary text serif whose curves all let daylight through, so it handles the reading while the heading handles the looking.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-cutive: Refined and literary at the text level, with something cooler up top. Arkhip draws every stroke at one thickness and floats its letters apart, while Cutive spreads its running text wide and lets each c open generously.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-david-libre: Cool, wiry geometry on top. Arkhip builds every letter from one stroke width and keeps them floating apart, and David Libre sits beneath it as a dignified serif whose terminals hang open, so the page moves from sleek to settled.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-enriqueta: Arkhip glides under the eye like bent wire, its letters spaced apart and its strokes never changing width. Enriqueta, a text serif with chalky curves that stop short of closing, can be sized up a touch.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-gentium-plus: Gentium Plus is a classic serif with the wide mouth of a pitcher in each c, refined and unhurried. Arkhip, meanwhile, is best at bold, bent-pipe display lines where its constant stroke width and spaced-out letters show, while Gentium Plus is best at carrying the quieter text below.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-gowun-batang: Pipe-clean geometry up top, with Arkhip's open c and monoweight skeleton floating each letter apart. Gowun Batang, a refined text serif with terminals cut back to leave a big gap, gives that sharp contrast a literary, bookish anchor.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-habibi: Arkhip is all gliding, floating letters with stems that match its hairlines, since it has none. Habibi, a text serif with a clear channel into each round letter, brings the editorial, traditional weight underneath.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-inika: One constant stroke width runs through every Arkhip letter, each set well apart with a c as open as a bent paperclip. Inika, a classic, traditional text serif with a see-through gap in each s, handles the text while Arkhip earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-kay-pho-du: Arkhip draws modern, geometric letters that float well apart, with a c as open as a bent paperclip. Kay Pho Du, a classic serif with breathing counters and the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen, is the one that settles into traditional text.
